answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable stake before it can submit work, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud. Creating a thousand velvet identities does not create a thousand cheap votes: each must lock scarce capital, and detected sybils lose it. Randomly assigning audits makes it harder to wander among easy targets, while delayed withdrawals prevent an attacker from reclaiming a marble-sized stake immediately after a scam. This raises the cost, though it cannot stop wealthy attackers outright.
